segments.title: Setting up the recording and giving the tempo
segments.summary: Check that the recorder is picking up voices, then the students ask for the faster numbers and a tempo is tapped off. Much of the text is ASR repetition.

segments.title: Fitting rolls to the tune: blues and the tango beat
segments.summary: Williams says rolls are chosen by judgment to fit the number, as in the St. Louis Blues roll. They go through the tango beat again.

segments.title: How to end a number and play the break
segments.summary: Cie asks how a drummer ends a blues. Williams explains going to the cymbal, the crush roll and rim shots into the break, and adding double raps while practicing.

segments.title: High Society introductions and bass-drum breaks
segments.summary: They try High Society and its bridge passages and introductions, and Williams says to let the bass drum lay out and hit one beat on the break. The rest of the passage is ASR loops.

segments.title: Two-fold marches and dropping down to the chorus
segments.summary: Cie asks how two-fold marches go. Williams plays snare and bass drum on a march (Maryland suggested), counts it and drops down to the chorus, then asks how to end it. Much of the text is garbled.

segments.title: Mazurkas and the very fast waltz
segments.summary: They discuss how mazurkas, a fast waltz, were played in time. Williams says they are counted in one and recalls playing one in the old WPA band.

segments.title: Practicing on a pad to build the wrists
segments.summary: Cie has no practice pad and they talk about making one from rubber. Williams advises constant practice on a pad with two sticks, whistling the tune, to strengthen the wrists, and talks about drum heads.

segments.title: Playing rags and show-band snare beats; Red Happy Bolton
segments.summary: Williams says beats are varied accordingly for rags. He recalls buck-and-wing dancing on old shows and show-band drummers' snare beats, including Red Happy Bolton at the Lyric Theatre.

segments.title: Breaking Sensation and Climax Rag
segments.summary: Cie asks how to break rags like Joplin's Sensation and Climax Rag. Williams answers mostly in demonstration, and says he played it with George Lewis.

segments.title: Stick position and ending rolls with the bass drum
segments.summary: After an offer of fruitcake, Cie wants a few more slow and crush rolls. Williams explains keeping the sticks close and counting four beats on the bass drum to come out of a roll.

segments.title: Hand position and left-handed drummers
segments.summary: Cie asks to review stick position, and they discuss the right-angle hand position and a left-handed set-up, mentioning Joe Watkins.

segments.title: Photographing the grip
segments.summary: Williams explains the fingers holding the stick (the first finger and thumb carry it, the third and fourth are free) while Cie photographs his hands and arranges the microphone.

segments.title: Goodbye
segments.summary: A parting exchange. Williams says he enjoyed the other night and must practice the tango beat.
